head: PDA Notes app brings the Newton notepad back on iPhone and iPad
dek: PDA Notes from Enfour recreates the notepad of Apple's 1990s Newton pen computer, drawn pixel for pixel, for iPhone and iPad. Out since 19 November for 19.99 dollars, it was #47 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 24 November.
details: You write with a finger, stylus or Apple Pencil and choose whether handwriting turns into typed text, stays as ink that wraps like words, or becomes shapes and sketches; you delete by scrubbing and start a new note by drawing a line across the page. It also has checklists, outlines, a call log, folders and search, and its Names, Dates and To Do views link to Contacts, Calendar and Reminders. Assist can set up a meeting from a written line, and Siri and Shortcuts can create, find and read notes. Notes move over Bluetooth to another device with PDA Notes or Enfour PDA; the listing shows no in-app purchases.
where: iPhone and iPad (iOS 18.6 or later), also Apple silicon Macs and Vision Pro, App Store, 19.99 dollars
means: If you miss handwriting-first notes or the Newton look, this is a one-time purchase with no subscription; if you want a free notes app, it isn't one.
todo: Look at the screenshots on the App Store page before buying: it's 19.99 dollars up front.
